question: Should OpenClaw accept `socket.drain` as an advertised Gateway event for session teardown notifications after the mechanical blockers are fixed?
rationale: The source fix is mechanical, but the PR creates a new public Gateway event and slow-consumer teardown behavior that should match maintainer protocol intent.

options.title: Accept with docs and repair
options.body: Keep the `socket.drain` feature, require the duplicate resolver/typecheck repair, and document the public payload and reason contract before merge.

options.title: Keep teardown private
options.body: Do not add a new advertised event, and close or redirect the PR toward existing documented session event surfaces.

options.title: Defer protocol direction
options.body: Pause this PR until a broader Gateway teardown/lifecycle event contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Accept with docs and repair
recommendation.body: Keep the `socket.drain` feature, require the duplicate resolver/typecheck repair, and document the public payload and reason contract before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He is a recent Gateway session lifecycle contributor and is the best available owner in the inspected history for deciding whether the public event contract should exist.
